text: A Hill cipher numbers the letters, cuts the message into blocks and mixes each block with a fixed table of numbers. Whole blocks of known letters give equations that pin the table.
Here the letters were numbered in 200 K1 to K3 word orders instead of A=0 to Z=25, with blocks of 2, 3 and 4, every alignment, plain or with an added vector.
7,200 settings, 557 consistent with every whole block; every one of them fails the known letters left over, and the best decryption lands 21 of 24.
